intent: Get the Shell tests workflow green again. The previous commit added `kcov` to its apt install step on the assumption it was packaged for Ubuntu; it is not, and CI went red in 34s on 'E: Unable to locate package kcov'. CI now skips jail-requiring suites with an announced reason, while the pre-push hook keeps running them for real on the developer machine, which has kcov.
scope: .github/workflows/shell-tests.yml: drop kcov from the install step; SKIP jail_args-marked suites with a printed reason
Non-goal: building kcov from source in CI -- minutes added to every run for a check the pre-push hook already performs on every push
Non-goal: any change to ci_mirror.sh, which runs these suites for real and is unaffected
Non-goal: weakening the empty-marker guard, which stays a hard failure
changes: The assumption that kcov was apt-installable was inferred, not verified, and CI disproved it in 34 seconds. Upstream (SimonKagstrom/kcov v43) publishes no prebuilt binary asset either, so apt is not merely a packaging gap.

CI now declares what it cannot do rather than pretending to check it -- the same trade the arch-tests job already makes for Arch-only tests. The skip prints 'SKIP <runner> (needs the kcov jail; enforced by pre-push)' so it is announced, never silent.
The enforcement is not lost: ci_mirror.sh runs the marked suites through the real jail on every push, and that gate is already proven to fail on a broken assertion.
The empty-jail_args guard remains a hard failure, so a misconfigured marker still turns CI red instead of being skipped.

verification.command: local simulation of the workflow step's loop over all six discovered runners
verification.evidence: 5 PASS (scripts/lib, digital_wellbeing, hosts, periodic_background, utils), 1 SKIP (features/lib), failed=0. Every discovered runner is accounted for -- none silently dropped.

verification.command: replace jail_args with comments+blank lines only, re-run the marker check, restore
verification.evidence: 'FAIL (empty marker) -> correctly detected'. The fail-closed guard survives the rewrite; git diff --stat empty after restore.
'E: Unable to locate package kcov' / 'Process completed with exit code 100' -- the failure this commit fixes, recorded as the measured reason for the redesign.

risks: The features/lib suite is now verified only by the pre-push hook, not by CI. A push made with --no-verify would land it unchecked. Acceptable because --no-verify is already forbidden by memories/git-rules.md, and the alternative (building kcov from source) taxes every CI run.

If a future contributor works on a machine without kcov, ci_mirror.sh's jailed branch cannot run there either; the jail already errors with 'Error: kcov is not installed' rather than passing silently.
rollback: git revert the commit; CI returns to attempting the kcov install and goes red again on the same apt error.
After rollback, confirm the shell-tests workflow fails at the install step, which is the symptom this commit removes.
